classification: EXPLORATORY RESEARCH NON-CANON NON-RUNTIME, UNCONSTRAINED CONCEPT GEOMETRY NOT QUALIFIED
deliberately_unconstrained: Number and shape of internal deck tiers
important_caveat: Initial 2226 layouts deliberately ignore pressure hull fit and all access/egress, structural and load-path qualification. A concept is not a buildable part of Wayfarer yet.
shared_seat_reference: Illustrative segmented 1.58m projected-length Kazbek-inspired shell, not fitted or qualified. Acceleration orientation is visually represented but no real g-load test.

designs.name: Tiered command
designs.idea: Pilot and Navigator forward/lower, Captain centred behind and raised; 3 supporting mission stations.
designs.tradeoff: Raised Captain could lose screen sightlines; tier access remains unresolved

designs.name: Triangular command cluster
designs.idea: Three command seats face a shared triangular decision area; specialist stations surround it.
designs.tradeoff: Denser primary cluster may obstruct mutual screens

designs.name: Horseshoe bridge
designs.idea: A curved crew arc surrounds open command space and a reachable shared workpoint.
designs.advantage: Shared situational awareness across all six roles
designs.tradeoff: Longer cross-bridge communication and no privileged Captain view

designs.name: Amphitheatre command
designs.idea: Flight stations on a low forward tier; Captain on a raised middle tier; three specialists on an even higher aft tier.
designs.advantage: Tiered command visibility and distinct specialist levels
designs.tradeoff: Multiple step changes may be awkward in weightlessness and faults

designs.name: Mission pods
designs.idea: Pilot/NAV paired; engineering and mission form a separate task pod; sensors and Captain form another.

designs.name: Split-level command
designs.idea: Two-level bridge: flight pair on lower forward deck; Captain and specialists on a separate elevated command gallery.
designs.advantage: Clear command oversight with specialist work physically separated
designs.tradeoff: Movement between tiers and direct reach difficult in emergency

designs.name: Central command well
designs.idea: Captain at the middle of an inward-facing cluster; Pilot/NAV split toward opposite sides of the view.
designs.advantage: Collective command coordination and captain access

designs.name: Panoramic observation arc
designs.idea: Broad forward crew crescent, one rear centre Captain and specialist group, designed around the view.
designs.advantage: Shared experience of the panorama and distributed external observation
designs.tradeoff: Larger lateral separation weakens urgent crew cross-checking

why: F1: directly provides raised centred Captain with forward Pilot/NAV pair and is simplest crew supervision topology
F3: strong crew interaction and shared information across a continuous open horseshoe
F6: true alternative with multiple physical levels and separated flight versus command responsibilities
assessment.not_proven: This is qualitative selection for discussion and user viewing, not measured human performance or a demonstrated optimum. The other five remain equally selectable.
assessment.next_real_test: Compare actual task movements and views in the 3D render; select a topology before applying 3D hull, circulation and g-load fit checks.
